commitResults.messageTitle: Reject pastes the command box would silently alter
commitResults.messageBody:
The command box drops pasted tabs and line breaks before parsing,
which can join words, change contact values or turn a near-miss
reply into a confirmation.

Let's reject the whole paste, show a warning and block Enter until
the command is edited, so the earlier text cannot be submitted by
mistake. A trailing line break at the end of the command is still
allowed, since dropping it joins nothing.

Fixes #351.

Let's drop that claim and add a test with a pending confirmation,
where an empty Enter would otherwise cancel. Also document in the

Align Developer Guide with course DG guidelines
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide had drifted from the course's DG requirements:
the manual-testing appendix repeated the User Guide and carried a team
release checklist, implementation sections listed validation rules and
error strings that the User Guide and code already define, several
sentences appeared twice, and unused AB3 undo/redo diagrams remained.

Let's make it explain design instead of restating behaviour:
- Condense the manual-testing appendix and merge its duplicated
  sections. Drop the release checklist, which Testing.md covers.
- Replace per-field validation rules and exact bulk-tag error strings
  with the reason validation lives in the model and shared parser.
- Add short design notes to help, sort, email search, show and
  tag/untag.
- Move Limitations to its own section and the verification roadmap
  under Development workflow. Both anchors are kept so existing User
  Guide links still work.
- Remove duplicated sentences in the saving, import and rename text.
- Renumber user stories in priority order and remap the use cases.
- Expand Common classes and use British spelling consistently.
- Delete unused AB3 undo/redo and tracing diagram sources and images.

No source code or User Guide content changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add import folder rule and release checks to DG
commitResults.messageBody:
Section 8 did not say that the packaged JAR only imports files from
inside its own folder, although FileUtil#resolvePath enforces it and
rejects symbolic links. When the manual-testing appendix was condensed
it also lost its checks for startup from a folder with spaces, screen
sizes, response time, User Guide examples and the symbolic-link case.

Let's record both:
- Add a folder-restriction bullet to section 8 that matches
  resolvePath: relative paths resolve from the JAR folder, a path that
  leaves it or passes through a symbolic link is rejected with its own
  message and changes nothing, an absolute path inside the folder is
  accepted, and development runs are unrestricted. Export applies the
  same check.
- Add a Release checks subsection to the manual-testing appendix
  covering startup from a folder with spaces, the folder restriction
  including a symbolic link, screen sizes (NFR05), response time
  (NFR08) and User Guide examples.

Documentation only.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show roster card names in composed Unicode form to avoid slow layout
commitResults.messageBody:
On macOS, a name that mixes CJK characters with a combining accent
(for example e followed by U+0301) made JavaFX spend tens of seconds
laying out the roster card. In timings with six such members, the
build and layout took about 45 seconds, and the first window resize
about 14 seconds. Removing either the CJK characters or the combining
mark made it fast again, and a 5,000-character ASCII name was fast
too, so length is not the cause.

Normalize the displayed name to NFC so a combining mark is recomposed
into a single character where one exists. The stored name and the
saved JSON are unchanged. With the change the same members laid out
in about 30 ms.

Names whose combining marks have no precomposed form, such as
Devanagari, are not helped. The details panel and other places that
show the name are not changed.

Addresses #378

commitResults.messageTitle: Use literal colors for filter chip styles
commitResults.messageBody:
The filter chip rules referenced -tc-sage and -tc-sage-soft, which are
defined on .root. When a chip is styled while detached from .root, such
as during window teardown on exit, JavaFX cannot resolve the lookups and
logs ClassCastException and 'Could not resolve' CSS warnings.

Replace the three lookups in the .filter-chip rules with the same literal
hex values so the chip no longer depends on inheriting from .root. The
rendered colors are unchanged.

Fixes #384

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the roster file in the permission save-failure message
commitResults.messageBody:
When the data folder is read-only, the AccessDeniedException message names
the internal temporary file that the atomic write creates beside the roster
(.trackcall-backup-*.tmp). LogicManager put that text into the user-facing
message, so users were pointed at a file they never created.

Add getSaveFailureDetails() so a permission failure reports the roster file
path from storage instead, and use it for the clear, import and general
save-failure messages. Other IO errors keep their existing text.

Update the two tests that expected the exception message to expect the
roster path for the permission case.

Fixes #382

displayed text, which is composed Unicode, so the clipboard matches
